Tuckman-Chang financial vulnerability flags

Source: R/outcomes.R
tuckman_chang.Rd

Tuckman and Chang (1991) call an organization financially vulnerable when it is in the most vulnerable quintile on any of four indicators: equity (net assets / revenue), revenue concentration (REVENUE_HHI), administrative costs (management and general / total expenses), and operating margin (surplus / revenue). Low equity, low administrative costs (little to cut), low margins, and high concentration are vulnerable. Greenlee and Trussel (2000) and Hager (2001) use the same four.

Usage

tuckman_chang(x, reference = x, by = "TAX_YEAR", q = 0.2)

Arguments

x

Organization-year table with REVENUE, SURPLUS, NET_ASSETS, REVENUE_HHI, and ADMIN_RATIO (from merger_measures() or panel_measures()).

reference

Table used for the cutoffs (default x).

by

Grouping columns for the cutoffs (e.g. c("TAX_YEAR", "NTEE_MAJOR")).

q

Quantile that defines the vulnerable tail.

Value

x with indicators TC_EQUITY, TC_HHI, TC_ADMIN, TC_MARGIN; flags TC_LOW_EQUITY, TC_HIGH_HHI, TC_LOW_ADMIN, TC_LOW_MARGIN; TC_N_OBS (indicators available), TC_N_FLAGS, TC_ANY (at least one flag), and TC_ALL (all four flagged; NA unless all four are available). The cutoffs are in attr(, "cutoffs").

Details

Cutoffs are quantiles computed within by groups of reference. Pass the full 990 panel (get_panel()) as reference, so merger organizations are ranked against all filers rather than against each other. The admin and concentration indicators need the full Form 990, so 990-EZ filers are flagged on equity and margin only.

References

Tuckman, H. P., & Chang, C. F. (1991). Nonprofit and Voluntary Sector Quarterly, 20(4), 445-460. Greenlee, J. S., & Trussel, J. M. (2000). Nonprofit Management and Leadership, 11(2), 199-210.
